You will work with our product and engineering teams in the UK and China, and with our manufacturing partners, to make sure every product launches right and stays right. A key focus is quality during new product development (NPD): running a gate review at each development stage to make sure major issues are solved and aligned, or that mitigation plans are in place for any open issues, before the product moves forward. Please note that this role will be situated at our office in Dongguan, China, working on-site from Monday-Friday. The normal working hours will be 9am - 6:30pm CST. 👋 About You Outgoing and proactive — you go to the production line and talk to people rather than wait for problems to come to you. Driven — you take ownership and push issues through to closure, even under deadline pressure. Persuasive with facts — you convince others with data and evidence, and hold a firm line while keeping good relationships. A clear communicator — you explain quality risks simply to the UK team, engineers, suppliers and managers, in Mandarin and English. 🔑 Key Responsibilities: Product validation (NPD) Define critical-to-quality characteristics, quality requirements and inspection standards for new products. Validate the the product validation plan with the UK team and our lab team (functional, reliability, drop and environmental tests) and make sure each build is tested against it. Review validation results, drive failures to root cause and verify fixes before the next build. Give design-for-manufacturing and DFMEA input to the design team. Mass production readiness Review tooling and first samples, and drive issues to closure with suppliers. Approve supplier quality control plans based on PFMEA; sign off limit and golden samples. Present validation and readiness evidence at launch gate reviews. Problem solving for production and after-sales Monitor production and test data; lead root cause analysis (8D, 5Why) and corrective actions with suppliers. Analyse returns and customer feedback, and feed the learnings back into design and standards. ✔️How will success be measured? Able to read GD&T drawings and analyse data with Minitab or Excel. Proven NPD product validation experience: planning validation and reliability tests (functional, drop, environmental), reviewing results and driving design fixes. Working knowledge of ISO 9001. Fluent Mandarin and good business English. Willing to travel regularly to supplier sites 🎉 Our Offer We work fully on-site in our custom Dongguan office so that we can retain the collaborative and vibrant Mous culture that people love. Professional Development: Training budget plus regular Mousterclasses to share expertise across teams. Charlie HR Perks: Access to exclusive perks and discounts via Charlie HR. Global Collaboration: Seamless remote collaboration with international teams, including weekly all-hands and virtual socials. 🐭 Our Values Get Results – We take accountability, prioritise impact, and push standards higher. Work Together – We collaborate openly, challenge constructively, and learn from each other. Enjoy the Ride – We stay agile, embrace change, and enjoy building something special together. 🌈 Our Commitment Mous is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate individuality and are committed to building a diverse team with a wide range of experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds.

review_candidates.title: Senior Maintenance Planner - Operational Readiness
review_candidates.description: The Senior Maintenance Planner - Operational Readiness is the first dedicated Processing Maintenance position for Assafou. Initially, the role will report directly to the Processing Manager and once appointed, the reporting line will transition to the Fixed Plant Maintenance Superintendent. The role will work closely with the Project team, Group Operational Support and Engineering, EPCM, Supply Chain, OEMs and commissioning specialists. From detailed design through commissioning, start-up and ramp-up, the role will develop the maintenance planning information and asset-management foundations required for operation This includes asset data, equipment criticality, maintenance strategy, job plans, equipment BOMs, spare-parts requirements, tooling, first fills, condition-monitoring requirements, asset integrity requirements and maintenance documentation. All maintenance readiness deliverables shall be developed in accordance with the Endeavour Mining Asset Management Policy, Framework, Group Standards and agreed maintenance governance requirements supporting asset management principles aligned with ISO 55000. Operational-readiness and commissioning experience is required to support the transition into the permanent maintenance organization. KEY ACCOUNTABILITY Maintenance planning, asset management & operational readiness: Maintain the Processing Maintenance readiness schedule within the planner scope, aligned with project milestones, commissioning, first ore and ramp-up. Coordinate maintenance-planning deliverables with the Processing Manager, Project and Group functions, and highlight gaps or late inputs that may affect commissioning, start-up or early operations. Apply Group Standards, maintenance governance requirements and operational-readiness processes throughout project development, commissioning and handover. Maintain visibility of maintenance-readiness risks, gaps and actions for issues that may affect commissioning, start-up or sustainable operation mining challenges. Develop predictive models for operational performance, resource estimation, or reconciliation, equipment productivity, and planning accuracy. Transform complex operational datasets into business insights that support data-driven decision making. Develop reusable analytics products and decision-support tools. Maintenance Management System and Master Data: Develop and maintain the plant asset hierarchy, equipment register, functional locations and maintenance master data required for the maintenance management system. Ensure asset hierarchy, equipment master data, maintenance strategies, BOMs and related maintenance data comply with Group Standards and agreed data governance requirements. Develop preventive and condition-based maintenance routines, digitalized task lists, lubrication management plans, frequencies and job plans using OEM information, asset criticality and Group standards. Prepare equipment bills of materials (BOMs) and ensure materials and spare parts are associated with the correct plant assets. Support the setup and progressive population of the maintenance management system and maintain accurate planning data as vendor and commissioning information becomes available. Prepare practical planning, scheduling and backlog-management templates and routines for use by the future maintenance team. Spare Parts, Materials, Tooling and First Fills: Review EPCM and OEM recommended spare-parts lists and recommend classification of commissioning, running, insurance and strategic spares. Identify critical and long-lead spare parts and support Supply Chain and Project Procurement with technical review and procurement tracking. Review opportunities for spare-parts commonality with existing Endeavour operations where practical. Design, commissioning and handover support: Participating in design reviews from a maintenance-planning and maintainability perspective, include equipment access, lifting and removal routes, isolation points, maintenance platforms and workshop requirements. Compile and organize vendor manuals, drawings, warranties, maintenance procedures, commissioning records and as-built information required for future maintenance planning. Start-up, Ramp-up and Transition to Operations: Support maintenance planning and scheduling during commissioning, first ore, start-up and ramp- up in coordination with the Processing Manager, commissioning team and developing maintenance organization. Provide a structured handover of open planning actions, master data, job plans and spare-parts information as the permanent maintenance organization is mobilized. Safety and Compliance: Ensure maintenance job plans include appropriate safety requirements, permits, isolations, lifting requirements and statutory inspection needs. Conduct planning activities in accordance with Endeavour Mining HSE standards and site procedures. Maintain accurate and traceable maintenance planning and handover records. SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE Education: Internationally recognized Degree or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline. An equivalent combination of technical qualifications and substantial relevant maintenance experience may be considered. Relevant experience: Minimum 10 years of progressive maintenance planning experience in mining or mineral processing, preferably in gold processing plants. Demonstrated maintenance operational-readiness experience on a greenfield or major brownfield process plant, with practical involvement through commissioning, start-up and ramp-up. Hands-on experience with CMMS, asset hierarchies, equipment master data, BOMs, preventive- maintenance routines, task lists and job plans. Working knowledge of asset-management systems and ISO 55000 principles. Practical knowledge of equipment criticality, maintenance strategy development, PM optimization, condition monitoring, asset integrity and reliability improvement. Experience reviewing critical and long-lead spare parts, vendor spare-parts recommendations and initial inventory requirements. Practical involvement in equipment commissioning, handover and early operational maintenance planning. Sound understanding of maintainability, shutdown planning and scheduling, work management, condition monitoring and maintenance performance indicators. Experience working with EPCM contractors, Project teams, Group Engineering / Asset Management, Supply Chain, OEMs and commissioning teams. Experience working in West Africa or a comparable operating environment is highly preferred. French / English language capability is advantageous.

review_candidates.title: Managing Director for a Health Workforce Initiative (Confidential)
review_candidates.description: SRI Executive Search has been contracted by the International Organization to assist with the search for an exceptional candidate to fill the position of Managing Director. Overview The World Health Organization projects a global shortfall of 11 million health workers by 2030, increasingly concentrated in the African region. This includes a shortage of nearly 900,000 midwives (Nove et al., 2021) and a similar gap in children's nurses, who make up only around 2% of the nursing workforce in several African countries, despite children comprising up to half the population (North et al., 2019). These shortages are closely linked to preventable maternal, newborn, and child deaths and high under-five mortality. WHO Afro modeling estimates that health workers required a $36.3 billion wage bill in 2022, against an available financing envelope of just $20.85 billion—a 43% workforce financing gap across the region's 47 countries. This constrained fiscal space is prompting governments and partners to rethink traditional workforce approaches, including how new technologies, such as AI-enabled tools for training, clinical decision support, and workflow efficiency, can extend the reach and impact of a limited workforce, while keeping health workers and human connection at the center of care. In May 2026, African governments adopted the Accra Declaration at the Africa Health Workforce Investment Forum, committing to concrete action on planning, training, and retaining the continent's health workforce. Against this backdrop, a multi-country health workforce initiative is being set up to strengthen the availability, quality, distribution, and retention of primary health care and maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) workers across the Africa region. The initiative will support government-led efforts to close these gaps — including shortages in nursing, midwifery, MNCH specialists, allied health cadres, and community health workers — that limit access to quality primary MNCH care. The initiative will be informed by a country-led planning process, partnering with governments, training institutions, and implementing organizations to strengthen health workforce policy, planning, and financing systems; expand and improve training capacity; support the equitable distribution and retention of health workers; and address gaps in medical equipment and facility infrastructure that limit health worker effectiveness and retention. A secretariat is being set up to provide technical, programmatic, and financial management assistance to participating governments and partners, including workforce planning and training design, monitoring and evaluation, and alignment with the initiative's technical framework and country priorities. The Managing Director (MD) will lead the programme and operational delivery of the initiative and act as its senior representative. The role will be employed through the host organization. The ideal candidate is a grant making expert with experience in funding or implementing ambitious global health programs in health systems strengthening in Africa including health workforce. It is essential that you submit your CV in English , specifically in Microsoft Word format (.doc/.docx), not exceeding 10MB. Applications in other languages or formats will not be considered. Rest assured, all information will be handled with the utmost confidentiality.
